glossary.Autoimmune: When the immune system attacks the body's own tissues.
glossary.Multisystem: Affecting several organ systems at once.
glossary.Mucosal ulcers: Sores in the lining of the mouth, nose or genitals.
glossary.Cutaneous vasculitis: Inflammation of small blood vessels in the skin, causing purpura or ulcers.
glossary.Pericarditis: Inflammation of the sac around the heart, causing sharp chest pain eased by sitting forward.
glossary.Neuropsychiatric lupus: Lupus affecting the brain or nerves, causing psychosis, seizures or severe headache.
glossary.Psychosis: Loss of contact with reality, such as hallucinations or delusions.
glossary.Transplacental: Crossing the placenta from mother to fetus.
glossary.Fetal bradycardia: An abnormally slow heart rate in the unborn baby.
glossary.Gestation: The time since conception, counted in weeks of pregnancy.
glossary.Coombs test: The direct antiglobulin test, detecting antibodies stuck to red cells in autoimmune haemolysis.
glossary.Proteinuria: Protein in the urine, a sign of kidney damage.
glossary.Nephritic: Kidney inflammation causing haematuria, hypertension and some proteinuria.
glossary.Creatinine: A muscle waste product cleared by the kidneys; a rise means worsening kidney function.
glossary.Coronary artery disease: Narrowing of the heart's arteries by atheroma.
glossary.Chronic discoid lupus erythematosus: Skin-limited lupus causing red, scaly, scarring plaques in sun-exposed areas.
glossary.Plaques: Raised, flat-topped skin lesions over 1 cm across.
glossary.Constitutional symptoms: Whole-body symptoms such as fever, fatigue and weight loss.
glossary.Urinalysis: Testing urine, usually by dipstick, for blood, protein and other substances.
glossary.Urine dipstick: A test strip dipped in urine that changes colour with protein, blood or glucose.
glossary.Glomerulonephritis: Inflammation of the kidney's filtering units (glomeruli).
glossary.Proliferative glomerulonephritis: Glomerulonephritis with an increased number of cells in the glomeruli.
glossary.Renal biopsy: Taking a small needle sample of kidney tissue to examine under the microscope.
glossary.C1q: The first component of the classical complement pathway, which binds immune complexes.
glossary.Titre: The concentration of an antibody in the blood.
glossary.Subacute cutaneous lupus: A photosensitive lupus rash of ring-shaped or scaly lesions, linked to anti-Ro.
glossary.Cytopenias: Low counts of one or more blood cell types.
glossary.Corticosteroids: Anti-inflammatory steroid drugs such as prednisolone.
glossary.Prednisolone: An oral corticosteroid used to control flares.
glossary.Immunosuppressant: A drug that dampens the immune system.
glossary.Cytotoxic: Toxic to dividing cells; used here to suppress immune cells.
glossary.Methotrexate: A folate antagonist DMARD used as a steroid-sparing agent.
glossary.Procainamide: An antiarrhythmic drug known to cause drug-induced lupus.
glossary.Histone: A protein around which DNA is wound inside the nucleus.
glossary.Immune tolerance: The immune system's normal ability not to attack the body's own molecules.
glossary.Nuclear antigens: Molecules from the cell nucleus, such as DNA and histones, targeted in lupus.
glossary.Idiopathic: Arising spontaneously or from an unknown cause.
glossary.Fibrosis: Replacement of normal tissue by scar tissue.
glossary.Conduction tissue: Specialised heart muscle that carries the electrical signal, including the AV node.
